Module np.cincuentazo
Package np.cincuentazo.model

Class Hand

java.lang.Object
np.cincuentazo.model.Hand
public class Hand extends Object
Represents the hand of cards held by a single player during the game.

Invariant

During active gameplay, a hand contains exactly 4 cards. This invariant is enforced by the game flow (the controller deals 4 cards at setup and ensures the player draws one replacement after every play), but it is not enforced by this class itself â€” the Hand is a pure data structure without game-rule knowledge.

Index stability

Cards are stored in an ArrayList so each card has a stable 0-based index. The UI maps visual card slots to these indices, so removing a card at index i shifts subsequent cards â€” the controller must re-render the hand after every removal.

  • Method Details

    • addCard

      public void addCard(Card card)
      Adds a card to the end of the hand.

      Called in two situations:

      1. During initial deal (4 times per player).
      2. After a player plays a card â€” they draw one replacement so the hand returns to the expected size.
      Parameters:
      card - the card to add; must not be null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if card is null

    • removeCard

      public Card removeCard(int index, int tableSum) throws InvalidPlayException
      Removes and returns the card at the given index.

      This is the primary play action: the player selects a card by its visual slot (index), the controller calls this method to retrieve it, and then places it on the table.

      Parameters:
      index - 0-based position in the hand
      Returns:
      the removed card
      Throws:
      IndexOutOfBoundsException - if index is negative or â‰¥ getHandSize()
      InvalidPlayException - if the card at index cannot legally be played given the current tableSum (checked variant so the controller must handle it explicitly)

    • removeAll

      public List<Card> removeAll()
      Removes all cards from the hand and returns them as a new list.

      Called when a player is eliminated: all their remaining cards must be sent to the bottom of the deck.

      Returns:
      a new list containing all cards that were in the hand; the hand is empty after this call

    • getPlayableCards

      public List<Card> getPlayableCards(int tableSum)
      Returns the subset of cards in this hand that can legally be played given the current table sum.

      A card is legally playable when tableSum + card.getValue(tableSum) â‰¤ 50. If the returned list is empty, the player has no valid move and is eliminated from the game.

      Parameters:
      tableSum - the current sum on the table
      Returns:
      a new, possibly empty, list of playable cards; order matches the hand's internal order

    • canPlay

      public boolean canPlay(int tableSum)
      Returns true if the player has at least one legally playable card.

      This is the fast-path check used at the start of every turn. If it returns false, the player is eliminated without needing to build the full playable list.

      Parameters:
      tableSum - the current sum on the table
      Returns:
      true if getPlayableCards(int) would return a non-empty list

    • getCards

      public List<Card> getCards()
      Returns an unmodifiable view of the cards in this hand.

      The view reflects the live state of the hand â€” if a card is later added or removed, the view will reflect those changes. Callers must not try to add or remove through the returned reference.

      Returns:
      an unmodifiable list of cards in hand order
